The **2024 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2023–24 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League"), the 69th season of Europe's premier club football tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), and the 32nd season since it was renamed from the [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") to the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). It was held at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England, on 1 June 2024,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-5) between German club [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") and Spanish club [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"). Due to the postponement and relocation of the [2020 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2020 UEFA Champions League final"), the final hosts were shifted back a year, with London instead hosting the 2024 final.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-6)
Real Madrid won the match 2–0 for [a record-extending 15th title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Cup_and_UEFA_Champions_League_records_and_statistics#General_performances "European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics"), and their sixth in eleven seasons.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-summary-7) As winners, they earned a spot to play in the [2024 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Super_Cup "2024 UEFA Super Cup"), against the winners of the [2023–24 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League"), [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_BC "Atalanta BC"). They also earned a chance to compete in the [inaugural edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_FIFA_Intercontinental_Cup "2024 FIFA Intercontinental Cup") of the [FIFA Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Intercontinental_Cup "FIFA Intercontinental Cup"). As they had already qualified for the [2025 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2025 FIFA Club World Cup") by winning the same tournament in 2022, the spot intended for the winners was redistributed via the UEFA club ranking, with Dortmund claiming one of those spots.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-:0-8)

## Venue
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Venue")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Wembley_Stadium_interior.jpg/330px-Wembley_Stadium_interior.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wembley_Stadium_interior.jpg)[Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") hosted the final.
This was the third UEFA Champions League final to take place at the rebuilt Wembley Stadium, having previously been held in [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2011 UEFA Champions League final") and 2013. Overall, it was the eighth final to be held in London, with the other five matches taking place at the [original Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_\(1923\) "Wembley Stadium \(1923\)") in [1963](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_European_Cup_final "1963 European Cup final"), [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_European_Cup_final "1968 European Cup final"), [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_European_Cup_final "1971 European Cup final"), [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_European_Cup_final "1978 European Cup final"), and [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_final "1992 European Cup final"). The match was the ninth European Cup final held in England, with the 2003 final having been held at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester"), equalling the record of nine European Cup finals held in each of Italy, Germany and Spain. It was also the thirteenth held in the United Kingdom, with the 1960, [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_European_Cup_final "1976 European Cup final") and 2002 finals held in Scotland and the 2017 final held in Wales.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-16) Wembley Stadium was also a host venue at [UEFA Euro 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020"), with eight matches played at the stadium including the semi-finals and [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020_final "UEFA Euro 2020 final").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17)
### Host selection
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Host selection")]
An open bidding process was launched on 22 February 2019 by UEFA to select the 2022 and 2023 UEFA Champions League final venues.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) Associations had until 22 March 2019 to express interest, and bid dossiers had to be submitted by 1 July 2019.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-AP-19)
[The Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") was reported to have bid with Wembley Stadium in London to host the 2023 final, in order to mark the centenary of the opening of the original stadium in 1923.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-AP-19) Wembley Stadium was selected by the UEFA Executive Committee during their meeting in [Ljubljana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ljubljana "Ljubljana"), Slovenia, on 24 September 2019,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20) where the hosts for the [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2021 UEFA Champions League final") and 2022 UEFA Champions League finals were also appointed.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21)
On 17 June 2020, the UEFA Executive Committee announced that due to the postponement and relocation of the [2020 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2020 UEFA Champions League final"), London would instead host the 2024 final.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-6)

### Borussia Dortmund
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Borussia Dortmund")]
See also: [2023–24 Borussia Dortmund season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Borussia_Dortmund_season "2023–24 Borussia Dortmund season")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/2023-08-12_TSV_Schott_Mainz_gegen_Borussia_Dortmund_%28DFB-Pokal_2023-24%29_by_Sandro_Halank%E2%80%93103.jpg/250px-2023-08-12_TSV_Schott_Mainz_gegen_Borussia_Dortmund_%28DFB-Pokal_2023-24%29_by_Sandro_Halank%E2%80%93103.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2023-08-12_TSV_Schott_Mainz_gegen_Borussia_Dortmund_\(DFB-Pokal_2023-24\)_by_Sandro_Halank%E2%80%93103.jpg)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/2023-08-12_TSV_Schott_Mainz_gegen_Borussia_Dortmund_%28DFB-Pokal_2023-24%29_by_Sandro_Halank%E2%80%93125.jpg/250px-2023-08-12_TSV_Schott_Mainz_gegen_Borussia_Dortmund_%28DFB-Pokal_2023-24%29_by_Sandro_Halank%E2%80%93125.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2023-08-12_TSV_Schott_Mainz_gegen_Borussia_Dortmund_\(DFB-Pokal_2023-24\)_by_Sandro_Halank%E2%80%93125.jpg)
[Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") defender [Mats Hummels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mats_Hummels "Mats Hummels") (left) and midfielder [Marco Reus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Reus "Marco Reus") (right) were the only players from the club's [2013 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2013 UEFA Champions League final") squad; Hummels scored the winner in the second leg of the semi-final against [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC") to book their place in the final, which was the last match for the club for both of them.
Borussia Dortmund qualified for the Champions League group stage by finishing as runners-up in the [2022–23 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Bundesliga "2022–23 Bundesliga"). In the group stage, they were drawn into Group F, alongside [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Ligue_1 "2022–23 Ligue 1") winners [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A "2022–23 Serie A") fourth-place team Milan and [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League "2022–23 Premier League") fourth-place side [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C."),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-GS_draw-22) which was widely regarded as the '[group of death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_of_death "Group of death")'.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-24)
In Dortmund's opener of the group stage, they faced Paris Saint-Germain at the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes") and lost 0–2, with goals from [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbapp%C3%A9 "Kylian Mbappé") and [Achraf Hakimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achraf_Hakimi "Achraf Hakimi").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25) On matchday 2, Dortmund drew in a 0–0 stalemate at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion") against Milan.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26) On matchday 3, Dortmund defeated Newcastle United away from home 1–0, with a goal from [Felix Nmecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Nmecha "Felix Nmecha").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-27) On matchday 4, Dortmund won 2–0 over Newcastle United at home, with goals coming from [Niclas Füllkrug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niclas_F%C3%BCllkrug "Niclas Füllkrug") and [Julian Brandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Brandt "Julian Brandt").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-28) On matchday 5, Dortmund got a 3–1 win against Milan at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"), with goals by [Marco Reus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Reus "Marco Reus"), [Jamie Bynoe-Gittens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Bynoe-Gittens "Jamie Bynoe-Gittens") and [Karim Adeyemi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karim_Adeyemi "Karim Adeyemi"), as [Samuel Chukwueze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Chukwueze "Samuel Chukwueze") got the temporary equaliser for the hosts.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-29) On matchday 6, returning to the Westfalenstadion, the hosts held Paris Saint-Germain to a 1–1 draw, with a goal from Adeyemi and a strike from [Warren Zaïre-Emery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Za%C3%AFre-Emery "Warren Zaïre-Emery") for the visitors.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30)
In the round of 16, Dortmund were drawn against Dutch club [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven"). In the first leg held at the [Philips Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philips_Stadion "Philips Stadion"), Dortmund drew 1–1, with goals from [Donyell Malen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donyell_Malen "Donyell Malen") and [Luuk de Jong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luuk_de_Jong "Luuk de Jong").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) In the reverse leg, Dortmund defeated PSV 2–0, with goals from [Jadon Sancho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jadon_Sancho "Jadon Sancho") and Reus, to win 3–1 on aggregate and advance to the quarter-finals.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-32)
In the quarter-finals, Dortmund were drawn against Spanish side [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid"). In the first leg, at the [Metropolitano Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitano_Stadium "Metropolitano Stadium"), the Germans suffered a 1–2 loss, with goals being scored by [Rodrigo De Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_De_Paul "Rodrigo De Paul"), [Samuel Lino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Lino "Samuel Lino") and [Sébastien Haller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Haller "Sébastien Haller"), whose late goal rescued Dortmund's chances for the progression.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-33) In the second leg, Dortmund produced a 4–2 win at home, trailing down 3–4 on aggregate in the second half and qualifying to the semi-finals 5–4 on aggregate, as Brandt, [Ian Maatsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Maatsen "Ian Maatsen"), Füllkrug, [Marcel Sabitzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcel_Sabitzer "Marcel Sabitzer"), [Mats Hummels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mats_Hummels "Mats Hummels") (own goal) and [Ángel Correa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Correa "Ángel Correa") got on the scoresheet.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34)
In the semi-finals, Dortmund were drawn against Paris Saint-Germain, making it a rematch of this season's group stage clash. In the first leg, at the Westfalenstadion, a lone winner from Füllkrug gave Dortmund a 1–0 victory.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35) In the second leg, at the Parc des Princes, the visitors won 1–0 once again, with the only goal of the match coming from Hummels. Dortmund won 2–0 on aggregate to qualify for their first Champions League final in eleven years.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-36)

"Manchester City F.C.") for the third consecutive season. The first leg at the Santiago Bernabéu ended in an intense 3–3 draw, in which goals from [Bernardo Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardo_Silva "Bernardo Silva"), [Phil Foden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Foden "Phil Foden"), and [Joško Gvardiol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo%C5%A1ko_Gvardiol "Joško Gvardiol") were denied by replies from a [Rúben Dias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%BAben_Dias "Rúben Dias") own goal, Rodrygo, and [Federico Valverde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Valverde "Federico Valverde").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-45) The second leg at the [City of Manchester Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium") also ended in a draw, as Rodrygo's early goal was cancelled out by a [Kevin De Bruyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_De_Bruyne "Kevin De Bruyne") equaliser. The match ended 1–1 after extra time and went into the penalty shootout to decide the winner after a 4–4 aggregate draw. It was Madrid's first Champions League shootout since the 2016 final. Goalkeeper [Andriy Lunin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Lunin "Andriy Lunin") saved two crucial penalties from Silva and [Mateo Kovačić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateo_Kova%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Mateo Kovačić"), with only [Luka Modrić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87 "Luka Modrić") missing his spot kick for the visitors, while [Antonio Rüdiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_R%C3%BCdiger "Antonio Rüdiger") scored the decisive final penalty to send his team to the semi-finals.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46)
In the semi-finals, Madrid were drawn against German champions Bayern Munich, the first "[European Clásico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayern_Munich%E2%80%93Real_Madrid_rivalry "Bayern Munich–Real Madrid rivalry")" since the [2017–18 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA Champions League") season. In the first leg at the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena"), a Vinícius double cancelled goals coming from [Leroy Sané](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leroy_San%C3%A9 "Leroy Sané") and [Harry Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kane "Harry Kane") for the hosts for a 2–2 draw.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-47) In the second leg at the Santiago Bernabéu, with Madrid initially trailing from an [Alphonso Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphonso_Davies "Alphonso Davies") goal, Joselu's double in the closing minutes of the game stunned the visitors to bring his team to a 2–1 victory in the match and 4–3 on aggregate, as they progressed to their sixth final in ten years.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48)

## Match
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Match")]
### Summary
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Summary")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/FC_RB_Salzburg_v.Real_Madrid_%28Testspiel%2C_7._August_2019%29_29.jpg/250px-FC_RB_Salzburg_v.Real_Madrid_%28Testspiel%2C_7._August_2019%29_29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FC_RB_Salzburg_v.Real_Madrid_\(Testspiel,_7._August_2019\)_29.jpg)[Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") defender [Dani Carvajal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Carvajal "Dani Carvajal") was named [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_match#Association_football "Player of the match") and became the first defender to score in a final since [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2016 UEFA Champions League final").
The match kicked off at 20:00 local time with an attendance of 86,212 fans. In the 21st minute, [Mats Hummels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mats_Hummels "Mats Hummels") played a pass to [Karim Adeyemi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karim_Adeyemi "Karim Adeyemi"), who rounded [Thibaut Courtois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thibaut_Courtois "Thibaut Courtois") by nudging the ball to the goalkeeper's right and attempting to shoot, but [Dani Carvajal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Carvajal "Dani Carvajal") tracked back to block his effort. Two minutes later, Adeyemi played a pass through the centre of the Madrid defence and released [Niclas Füllkrug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niclas_F%C3%BCllkrug "Niclas Füllkrug"), who struck the woodwork. Dortmund then produced a counter-attack after Brandt played a pass to Adeyemi, who was unable to beat Courtois from a tight angle, with the latter stretching out to make the initial parry, before saving Füllkrug's follow-up attempt. There were four minutes of added time after a series of [pitch invasions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_invasion#Association_football "Pitch invasion") earlier in the match.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-SportingNews-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-TheGuardian-54)
Neither side made any lineup changes during the interval. In the 49th minute, [Toni Kroos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Kroos "Toni Kroos") whipped in a free kick towards the Dortmund penalty area, with Carvajal sending his header over the bar. Madrid continued their pressure as [Vinícius Júnior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin%C3%ADcius_J%C3%BAnior "Vinícius Júnior") whipped a cross towards the penalty area, which [Nico Schlotterbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Schlotterbeck "Nico Schlotterbeck") nodded straight to Carvajal, whose half-volley effort was blocked by [Ian Maatsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Maatsen "Ian Maatsen"). Dortmund pushed again for a goal as Adeyemi played a cross into the penalty area towards Füllkrug, who managed to direct a powerful header that was saved by Courtois. Vinícius played another cross from the left flank to former Dortmund midfielder [Jude Bellingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude_Bellingham "Jude Bellingham"), who missed the ball which flew inches wide of the post. Dortmund then made their first substitution of the final, as Adeyemi came off for [Marco Reus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Reus "Marco Reus").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-SportingNews-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-TheGuardian-54)
With 15 minutes to go, Carvajal gave Madrid the lead in the 74th minute, heading in Kroos' corner from the left. Madrid had another chance to score, with [Eduardo Camavinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Camavinga "Eduardo Camavinga") cutting the ball back from the byline on the left to Bellingham, who looked to strike the ball past [Gregor Kobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregor_Kobel "Gregor Kobel"), only for Schlotterbeck to block his effort. Dortmund then made two attacking changes, as captain [Emre Can](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emre_Can "Emre Can") and [Julian Brandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Brandt "Julian Brandt") came off for [Donyell Malen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donyell_Malen "Donyell Malen") and [Sébastien Haller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Haller "Sébastien Haller"). Madrid came close to scoring a second again, as Kobel saved Camavinga's effort from outside the box and [Nacho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacho_\(footballer,_born_1990\) "Nacho \(footballer, born 1990\)")'s header from a Kroos corner.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-SportingNews-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-TheGuardian-54)
In the 83rd minute, Maatsen played a pass that was intercepted by Bellingham, who teed up Vinícius to his left, with the latter taking a touch and putting the ball past Kobel to double Madrid's lead. Madrid then made their first changes as Bellingham and Kroos came off for [Joselu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joselu "Joselu") and [Luka Modrić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87 "Luka Modrić"). Dortmund made their last substitution, with [Jadon Sancho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jadon_Sancho "Jadon Sancho") brought off for [Jamie Bynoe-Gittens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Bynoe-Gittens "Jamie Bynoe-Gittens"). Dortmund thought they had pulled one back, as Malen played a cross into the penalty area to Füllkrug, who powered a header into the left-hand side of the net, leaving Courtois with no chance. However, the goal was immediately disallowed by the referee after Füllkrug was shown to be in an offside position. Madrid made their two other substitutions in stoppage time, with [Rodrygo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrygo "Rodrygo") and Vinícius brought off for [Éder Militão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89der_Milit%C3%A3o "Éder Militão") and [Lucas Vázquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_V%C3%A1zquez "Lucas Vázquez"). The match ended after five minutes of stoppage time, with Madrid winning 2–0.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-SportingNews-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-TheGuardian-54)

## Post-match
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Post-match")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Carlo_Ancelotti_2016_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Carlo_Ancelotti_2016_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carlo_Ancelotti_2016_\(cropped\).jpg)[Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF")'s [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti") won his fifth Champions League title as a manager and seventh overall.
With the win, Real Madrid secured their record-extending 15th European Cup/Champions League title, and their sixth in the previous eleven seasons. It maintained Madrid's perfect final record in the Champions League era with nine wins, having last lost the final in 1981.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF-9) Madrid won the Champions League [unbeaten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Cup_and_UEFA_Champions_League_records_and_statistics#Unbeaten_sides "European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics") for the first time, with nine wins and four draws.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-summary-7) They also completed their fifth [European double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_\(association_football\) "Double \(association football\)") (after [1956–57](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956%E2%80%9357_Real_Madrid_CF_season "1956–57 Real Madrid CF season"), [1957–58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957%E2%80%9358_Real_Madrid_CF_season "1957–58 Real Madrid CF season"), [2016–17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2016–17 Real Madrid CF season") and [2021–22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2021–22 Real Madrid CF season")), having won the [2023–24 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_La_Liga "2023–24 La Liga").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58)
Four Madrid players (Dani Carvajal, Toni Kroos, Luka Modrić, and Nacho) equalled [Paco Gento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paco_Gento "Paco Gento")'s record of winning six European Cup/Champions League titles; all but Kroos have won all six of their titles with Real.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-59) In addition, Carvajal joined Gento as the only players to start in six different winning finals in the competition. Madrid manager Carlo Ancelotti extended his record as the [most successful manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_Cup_and_UEFA_Champions_League_winning_managers "List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League winning managers") in the competition's history, with his fifth title, and his third in charge of _Los Blancos_.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-60)
Meanwhile, Borussia Dortmund manager [Edin Terzić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edin_Terzi%C4%87 "Edin Terzić") stepped down from his role on 13 June 2024, nearly two weeks after losing the final. He stated that after the final, he asked for a meeting with the club's senior management team because he felt that "the club's new era should begin with a new man on the touchline", and wished Dortmund the very best.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-61) The next day, Terzić's assistant and former Dortmund player [Nuri Şahin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuri_%C5%9Eahin "Nuri Şahin") was appointed as head coach on a three-year contract.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-62)
### Crime
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Crime")]
After the game, the [Metropolitan Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police "Metropolitan Police") said that over 2,000 officers had been on duty for the game. 53 arrests had been made, mainly for trying to enter the stadium without a ticket and five arrests for entering the field of play. The game had only just kicked off when pitch invaders approached a number of the players.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-63)
Three people were later charged with entering the field of play contrary to Section 4 of the [Football (Offences) Act 1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_\(Offences\)_Act_1991 "Football \(Offences\) Act 1991"). Their court appearances were arranged for June and July 2024. The police said that most attempts to gain access to the ground without a ticket had been thwarted following an investment of £5 million, on new security lanes, improved fencing, additional stewards and ticket checks and their increased enforcement of the [public spaces protection order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_spaces_protection_order "Public spaces protection order"), carried out after the mass unrest at the Euro 2020 final in July 2021.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64) A Russian vlogger, Andrey Burim, was later reported to have offered 30 million [rubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruble "Ruble") to anyone who entered the pitch with his handle on their t-shirts.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-65) On 3 June, a Ukrainian man pled guilty at [Westminster Magistrates' Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster_Magistrates'_Court "Westminster Magistrates' Court") to entering the field of play and admitted he was inspired by Andrey Burim. He was fined £1,000, which was cut to £660 following his guilty plea. He was also ordered to pay £85 costs and a £264 witness surcharge.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66)
## Broadcasting
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Broadcasting")]
In Spain, the final was broadcast by [Televisión Española](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Televisi%C3%B3n_Espa%C3%B1ola "Televisión Española") (TVE), with an average of 6.1 million viewers (48.8% of share) and a peak of 7.3 million (52.5% of share) at 22:44 [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-:1-67) In total, at least 10.4 million unique viewers watched the match at some point.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-:1-67) In addition, public streaming service [RTVE Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTVE_Play "RTVE Play") gathered almost 800,000 unique viewers, with a total of 1.5 million views.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-:1-67) Post-match celebrations were followed by 3.2 million people.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-:1-67) Likewise, the [Movistar Plus+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movistar_Plus+ "Movistar Plus+") subscription platform broadcast the match, gathering 655,000 viewers.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-68)
